subject: Maths
pacing_note: The IEB publishes no ATP equivalent; term placement and week spans are the DBE ATP pacing carried over as a default. IEB schools set their own pacing — treat weeks as advisory.
assessment_note: DBE SBA programmes, control-test scopes and exam structures are deliberately stripped: IEB assessment is specified by the IEB Subject Assessment Guidelines (see ../exam_guidelines/), which have not been ingested yet. Do not fall back to the CAPS exam_structure for IEB papers.
scope_deltas: SAG-stated content-scope differences vs the CAPS/DBE prescription are recorded in scope_deltas.json in this folder (hand-maintained, SAG-transcribed only; an empty ledger means 'not yet transcribed', never 'no differences').

topics.name: Number patterns, sequences and series
subtopics: Revise number patterns with a constant second difference (quadratic general term)
Arithmetic and geometric sequences and series
Sigma notation
Derive and apply sum formulae for arithmetic and geometric series, including the sum to infinity of a convergent geometric series (−1<r<1)

topics.name: Functions: Formal definition, inverses, exponential and logarithmic
subtopics: Definition of a function
Inverse of a function; restricting the domain to obtain a one-to-one function
Determine and sketch inverses of y=ax+q, y=ax², y=bˣ (b>0, b≠1)
Graph characteristics: domain and range, intercepts, turning points, minima/maxima, asymptotes, shape and symmetry, average gradient, increasing/decreasing intervals
Revise the exponential function and exponential laws
Definition of a logarithm: y=log_b x ⇔ x=bʸ (b>0, b≠1)
Graph of y=log_b x for 0<b<1 and b>1

topics.name: Trigonometry
subtopics: Compound angle identities: sin(α±β), cos(α±β)
Double angle identities: sin2α, the three forms of cos2α
Revise proofs of the sine, cosine and area rules
Solve problems in two and three dimensions using the sine, cosine and area rules

topics.name: Euclidean Geometry
subtopics: Revise necessary and sufficient conditions for polygons to be similar
Prove: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally (Mid-point Theorem as special case of the converse)
Prove: equiangular triangles are similar
Prove: triangles with sides in proportion are similar
Prove: the Pythagorean Theorem by similar triangles

topics.name: Analytical Geometry
subtopics: Revise: equation of a line through two points; through one point parallel/perpendicular to a given line; inclination of a line (m=tanθ, 0°≤θ≤180°)
Equation of a circle (x−a)²+(y−b)²=r²
Equation of a tangent to a given circle

topics.name: Differential Calculus, including polynomials
subtopics: Factorise third-degree polynomials; remainder and factor theorems (degree ≤ 3, no proofs)
Intuitive understanding of the limit concept
Derivative from first principles for f(x)=ax²+bx+c, ax³, a/x and constants
Differentiation rules: d/dx(axⁿ)=anxⁿ⁻¹; sum/difference and constant-multiple rules
Equations of tangents to graphs of functions
Second derivative and concavity
Sketch cubic polynomial graphs: stationary points, points of inflection, x-intercepts (factor theorem)
Practical optimisation and rates of change, including calculus of motion

topics.name: Finance, growth and decay (continuation)
subtopics: Revise simple and compound growth and decay formulae A=P(1±in), A=P(1±i)ⁿ (incl. straight-line and reducing-balance depreciation)
Present value and future value annuities
Use logarithms to calculate n (the time period)
Critically analyse investment and loan options (including pyramid schemes)

topics.name: Statistics
subtopics: Revise: histograms, frequency polygons, ogives, variance and standard deviation (ungrouped), symmetric and skewed data, outliers
Bivariate data: scatterplots, least squares regression line, correlation; interpolation, extrapolation, skewness commentary

topics.name: Counting and probability
subtopics: Revise: addition rule, mutually exclusive events, complementary rule, independent events and the product rule
Venn diagrams up to three events; tree diagrams; two-way contingency tables
Fundamental counting principle
Probability problems using counting techniques
